subject: Sporadic tail latency -> renewal uplift & contingency credits discussion
messages:
From: Grace Hopper <grace.hopper@fincentric.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex.reed@fincentric.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:12:00Z
Subject: Intermittent tail latency impacting API-driven payouts - urgent

Hi Priya,

Over the last two weeks we've started seeing sporadic tail latency spikes on the Redwood endpoint (model: rwd-xt-xl) that are affecting our end-of-day payout jobs. Most requests are sub-200ms, but ~0.5-1% of calls spike beyond 2.5s and occasionally timeout in our box pipelines. That pattern caused three manual retries and one delayed payout batch on Friday (logs attached).

This is a renewal-sensitive situation: our contract renews mid-Jan and the product team is pushing for a reliability uplift (we're evaluating premium SLA options). Before escalating to procurement, could you outline:
- immediate mitigations you can enable (routing, priority pool)
- any temporary credits or exceptions you can offer for the outages
- what a premium SLA (latency SLO and enforcement) would look like and cost delta

We have a short window to decide whether to expand to dedicated capacity or stay on hosted with premium guarantees. Can we set up a 30-minute call Monday to align?

Thanks,
Grace
Head of Platform Engineering
FinCentric

Attachments: latency-digests.zip (logs and traces)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Hopper <grace.hopper@fincentric.com>, Alex Reed <alex.reed@fincentric.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail latency impacting API-driven payouts - urgent

Hi Grace — thanks for the data and the clear summary. We're sorry for the disruption.

Short-term: we can enable routing of your traffic to a higher-priority host pool and temporarily bump your concurrency limits to reduce queuing. Marcus can also enable prefix/KV cache warming for your most common prompt families. We'll stand up an incident war room tonight to baseline.

Medium-term: we can offer a 60-day pilot of our Premium SLA (99.95% availability and defined tail latency targets) plus a one-time account credit to compensate for the observed incidents. I'll propose options on cost and credit on our Monday call.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Monday 2026-12-07 17:00 UTC to review mitigation, walk Marcus/Dylan through the logs, and agree on a pilot/credit figure.

I attached a short runbook so your SREs know what we'll change.

— Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Priya Natarajan | priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0142

Attachment: initial-runbook.pdf
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent tail latency impacting API-driven payouts - FinCentric (action items)

Team — forwarding FinCentric's logs and the customer's note. They see ~0.5-1% calls with >2.5s tail latency causing downstream retries. They are renewal-sensitive and want: immediate mitigations, a 60-day premium SLA pilot, and a proposed credit for the incidents.

Can you please:
- Dylan: quick triage on likely causes (queueing vs cold KV cache vs model kernel selection) and a short mitigation plan we can activate immediately.
- Marcus: estimate effort and cost to route them to a priority pool and to pre-warm caches for their top 20 prompts.
- Laura: commercial: draft two pricing options (premium hosted + SLA cost delta; dedicated pool estimate) and a recommended one-time credit figure (range).

Goal: come back by EOD 2026-12-06 so I can confirm Monday's call with the customer.

Thanks,
Priya
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent tail latency impacting API-driven payouts - FinCentric (action items)

Quick triage notes (summary of my read of the traces):
- Spikes line up with bursts of large payloads and a small subset of prompts that trigger longer decode paths. Not typical warm-start issues; KV/cache miss amplification looks likely for their pattern.
- We see occasional kernel fallback on some GPU types when sequence length briefly exceeds the usual batch; that causes a 2.0–3.0s jump.

Immediate mitigations we can flip today (low risk):
1) Route FinCentric to the priority pool (isolated hosts) — removes noisy neighbor queueing.
2) Enable prefix/KV cache pre-warming for their top 20 prompt hashes.
3) Force a quantization-friendly kernel path for the short term to avoid fallback.

Estimated delivery: routing and config flips ~2–4 hours (ops-run), cache pre-warm ~4–8 hours to seed, kernel override requires canary smoke testing but should be reversible within the weekend. Cost: routing to priority pool increases per-token cost ~12–18% for the pilot window.

I'll produce a short PDF with the analysis and step-by-step ops commands for the war room.

— Dylan
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: tail-latency-analysis.pdf
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@fincentric.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Grace Hopper <grace.hopper@fincentric.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail latency impacting API-driven payouts - urgent

Thanks Priya and team — appreciate the quick triage.

We're open to the 60-day pilot of the Premium SLA, but two asks before we sign:
1) One-time incident credit to cover our operational costs from the last two recurrences — we're thinking 10% of last month's invoice as a starting point.
2) A clearer SLA addendum that defines tail latency SLOs (p95/p99 target and remediation credits) and the rolloff to Dedicated if the pilot doesn't hit targets.

If Redwood can commit to those two items and the routing/caching changes tonight, we will provisionally accept the pilot and won't move to procurement immediately. We want the addendum and credit nailed down in writing before the pilot starts.

Happy to discuss on Monday as scheduled.

— Alex
Director of Engineering, FinCentric
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@fincentric.com>, Grace Hopper <grace.hopper@fincentric.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T15:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail latency impacting API-driven payouts - urgent (SLA addendum & credits)

Alex / Grace — thanks for the clear asks. Summary and our commitment: 

1) Immediate mitigation: Dylan's team will route your traffic to the priority pool tonight and start cache pre-warming. Marcus will send the ops knobs and ETA in a separate note.

2) Credit: Redwood proposes a one-time operational credit equal to 15% of your November invoice (we believe this fairly compensates the retries and engineering overhead while recognizing our mitigation costs). If you'd like to counter-propose 10%, we will consider it; happy to confirm on Monday's call.

3) SLA addendum (draft): we've prepared a short addendum that specifies 99.95% availability plus p95 < 300ms and p99 < 900ms for the Premium SLA during typical production loads; remediation credits tiered above 99.90. The addendum also includes a 60-day pilot clause: if SLOs are not met for two consecutive weeks, you can either (a) convert to Dedicated with migration support, or (b) terminate pilot without penalty. Draft attached.

4) Commercials: Laura will join the call with two pricing options (hosted premium and dedicated pilot). We'll also include the DocuSign link to sign the addendum once agreed.

Proposed meeting confirmation: Monday 2026-12-07 17:00 UTC — note that was the initially proposed time; if that doesn't work for you, send alternatives and we'll move.

We want to make this low friction so you can focus on product. Thanks for working through this with us.

— Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Priya Natarajan | priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
